$comment: Prompt manifest for tools/gen-art.mjs. Output: assets/art/<id>.png. Style keys keep 40 images in two coherent looks. `reference` = ids of already-generated images to use as style anchors (edits endpoint). See docs/art-pipeline.md. Styles with `key` are rendered opaque on that chroma colour and keyed out by the tool (see tools/gen-art.mjs). `owner-cat` is a personal photo in art/refs (gitignored, not in the repo).

garden.prefix: Soft watercolor storybook illustration for a cheerful card game: painterly, gentle edges, warm sunlit colours (buttery yellow, leaf green, cream, sky blue). The subject is a cute, friendly CYBORG garden creature: visible brass gears, tiny glass lenses, springs and copper wire integrated into its body, gentle happy expression. Centered, full body, clean silhouette, no text, no border.
garden.suffix: Isolated on a fully transparent background: no scenery, no foliage, no backdrop, no vignette, no ground shadow.

thicket.prefix: Grim, photorealistic painted illustration for a folk-horror card game, like a diseased taxidermy specimen: photobashed painterly texture, low-key lighting, heavy film grain, desaturated palette of near-black greens, umber and bruised purple, a single cold rim light and a faint warm spill from the front. The creature is sick and wrong and disgusting: mangy fur wet and clumped, large patches of bare greasy grey skin with weeping sores and scabs, ribs and spine pushing through, crusted eyes that glow amber, drool, cracked yellow teeth, an unsettling hunched posture. The whole creature is ONE connected silhouette: every leg joins the body, every paw joins a leg, the tail joins the rump. No floating or detached parts. Gross and gory is welcome: open wounds, skin torn away over wet red muscle, exposed bone; wounds are red and pink, never amber or orange (only the eyes glow amber). Very dark overall: near-black fur, crushed blacks, muted desaturated colour, like a photograph taken by one dim lamp; the only bright things are the amber eyes and the wet red of the wounds. Centered, full body, no text, no border.
thicket.suffix: Isolated on a fully transparent background: no backdrop, no halo, no ground, no vignette.

thicket-morbid.$comment: The thicket look WITHOUT the gore (2026-09-18, the owner: gory does not have to be in everything - just dark, morbid and evil). Same lighting, grain and palette as thicket; the horror is in the anatomy, the fur, the eyes and what the creature carries, never in wounds. The spider uses it.
thicket-morbid.prefix: Grim, photorealistic painted illustration for a folk-horror card game, like a diseased taxidermy specimen: photobashed painterly texture, low-key lighting, heavy film grain, desaturated palette of near-black greens, umber and bruised purple, a single cold rim light and a faint warm spill from the front. The creature is sick and wrong and unsettling: mangy fur wet and clumped, greasy skin, crusted eyes that glow amber, an unsettling hunched posture. The whole creature is ONE connected silhouette: every leg joins the body, every paw joins a leg. No floating or detached parts. NO GORE: no wounds, no sores, no blood, no exposed muscle, bone or ribs, no red anywhere on the body - the skin and fur are unbroken; the horror is in the anatomy, the eyes and what the creature carries. Very dark overall: near-black fur, crushed blacks, muted desaturated colour, like a photograph taken by one dim lamp; the only bright things are the amber eyes. Centered, full body, no text, no border.
thicket-morbid.suffix: Isolated on a fully transparent background: no backdrop, no halo, no ground, no vignette.

scene.prefix: Wide painterly environment for a card game table scene. Foreground is a bright, sunlit storybook garden of flowers, moss and pebbles; with depth it turns into grim painted realism: wet black soil, tangled roots, thorns, cobwebs and shadow where faint amber eyes watch. Heavy film grain on the far half only, vignette, no characters, no text.

thicket-object.prefix: Grim, photorealistic painted illustration for a folk-horror card game: photobashed painterly texture, low-key lighting, heavy film grain, desaturated palette of near-black greens, umber and bruised purple, a single cold rim light and a faint warm spill from the front. The subject is an OBJECT from a dark thicket, not a creature: dirty, damp, wrong. Centered, whole object in frame, no text, no border.
thicket-object.suffix: Isolated on a fully transparent background: no backdrop, no halo, no ground, no vignette.

assets.prompt: A spindly spider seen from the front and slightly above, its body bloated and glistening, with eight very long thin legs that all radiate from and clearly attach to its body, eight amber eyes, strands of dirty web trailing from it.

A scorpion of black chitin seen in side view, its shell crusted with grime and pale fungal blotches, tail raised high over its back and clearly attached, all eight legs and both pincers attached to its body, a bead of venom glowing faintly at the sting, amber eyes.

The Greeble: a small hunched creature made of shadow and television static, its outline smeared and indistinct but forming one single connected shape, only a pair of amber eyes and a wide grin of small teeth are certain, clutching a stolen breadcrumb in two thin hands.

A rat king: five or six gaunt mangy rats fused at their knotted tails into one writhing crown-shaped mass, their bodies radiating outward from the knot, seen from the front, many amber eyes, one rat wearing a tiny bent tin crown. IMPORTANT: the mass is shown floating in empty space against a flat, evenly lit, bright neon green chroma-key screen, cut out like a sticker, with a generous margin of the same green on every side including below it; the bottom edge of the image is exactly the same bright green as the top edge. The green is a perfectly flat digital colour fill, as if the mass had been pasted onto a solid colour layer in an image editor: no ambient occlusion, no cast shadow, no glow and no darkening of the green anywhere, not even right next to the outline. There is NO floor, NO ground, NO shadow, NO dark gradient, NO wall, table or cabin anywhere - only the creatures themselves are dark.

A huge hairy wolf spider seen from the front, forelegs raised, all eight legs clearly attached to its body, coarse wet bristles, fangs dripping, eight amber eyes in two rows. No web, no cobweb, no fog, no mist and nothing translucent anywhere in the image.

An enormous bear rearing upright on its hind legs and facing the viewer, front paws raised with claws catching the light, all four limbs clearly attached to its body, fur hanging in ragged wet clumps with large bare patches of greasy grey skin and weeping sores on its chest and belly, ribs showing, muzzle open over cracked yellow teeth with a string of drool, both eyes clearly visible: one milky white, one glowing amber; whole body visible from head to hind paws with a margin around it.

A gaunt moose standing in three-quarter view, all four legs clearly attached and planted, antlers like dead branches strung with cobweb, hide hanging off its ribs in patches, amber eyes, looming, whole body visible from antler tips to hooves with a margin around it.
A friendly elderly cyborg snail carrying a tiny wooden market stall on its shell, lanterns hanging from the awning, wearing spectacles.

The view across a low garden bed toward the woods, seen from a bug's height: a sunlit foreground of flowers, moss and pebbles that recedes into a dark thicket in the distance. No furniture, no wooden table, no man-made objects.
A top-down garden map: winding dirt trails between flower beds, a pond, a fence, and at the far edge a dark forest.

Drill Worm, a cyborg earthworm cousin of Wormillion: segmented pink worm body, a spinning brass drill bit where its head cap would be, small brass goggles pushed up, a determined grin, boring into a pebble with grit flying.
A cyborg roly poly (pill bug) caught mid-leap: riveted brass armour plates flaring open, tiny spring-loaded legs, one glass lens eye, an eager gleeful expression.
A small chubby cyborg caterpillar with copper-wire bristles, mouth wide open taking an enormous bite out of a leaf, cheeks stuffed, leaf crumbs flying, blissful.
A cyborg ladybug in flight with red enamel wing cases open, launching a burst of glowing brass-rimmed spots from its back like tiny cannonballs, trailing sparkles.

A cyborg BUTTERFLY as the single large subject filling the frame: an insect with two pairs of big stained-glass wings held in a fine brass frame, a slim segmented body, clockwork antennae, one glass lens eye. Its wings are swept forward mid-flap, scattering glittering golden dust; quick, playful, radiant.
A cyborg chameleon with a telescopic brass eye, its long pink tongue snapping out in a whip-crack across the frame, the tongue tip a brass ring, intensely focused.

The same real ginger tabby cat as the reference photo (orange tabby stripes, white chin and bib, pink nose) as a cyborg mid-pounce: front paws stretched out, one glowing brass-rimmed lens eye wide, tail straight out behind, fierce and adorable.
A tangled clump of old cobweb: thick grey silk strands wound into a sticky knot with a few loose strands trailing, dust, dew and the dry husks of two dead flies caught in it.

The Snail's market stall at the side of a sunlit garden path, seen head-on from a bug's height: a small rickety wooden stall with a striped cloth awning and paper lanterns, shelves of jars, brass gears and glass lenses behind, and an EMPTY wooden counter running across the lower third of the picture with nothing on it. Flowers and moss around the stall; past it the path runs away into a dark thicket where faint amber eyes watch. No characters, no snail, no text.

The inside of a sheltered fold of a huge sunlit leaf, seen from a bug's height: a half-spun cocoon of pale gold silk glowing with warm light hangs at the centre, silk threads and dew drops around it, soft moss below. Through the opening of the leaf the garden fades into a dark thicket where faint amber eyes watch. Hushed, warm, safe. No characters, no text.

A cyborg roly poly (pill bug) mid-molt: climbing out of its old riveted brass armour shell, which sits split open and empty beside it, its new shell soft and pale cream with the rivets not yet fitted, a loose spring popping out, a relieved happy grin.

A cyborg roly poly (pill bug) with riveted brass armour plates rummaging happily through leaf litter, a tiny brass lantern strapped to its head, holding up a golden bread crumb in two front legs like treasure, delighted.

A happy wriggling heap of many small cheerful cyborg earthworms, each a short segmented pink worm with a domed brass cap and one round glass lens eye, tumbling over one another in a pile, all smiling, no legs on any of them.

A fuzzy green cyborg caterpillar with copper-wire bristles and clockwork legs, cheeks puffed and eyes squeezed shut with effort, releasing a billowing pale yellow-green stink cloud from a small brass valve on its back, little wavy stink lines, comic and cheerful.

A cyborg chrysalis hanging from a leaf stem by a small brass hook: a teardrop of pale gold silk wrapped in fine brass bands, a tiny round glass porthole showing a sleeping smiling face inside, a small clockwork dial on its side ticking, soft glow.

A cheerful cyborg earthworm diving head-first into dark garden soil: only the back half of its segmented pink body and a small copper spring at the tail tip still show above ground, a spray of soil crumbs and pebbles flying up, a tiny brass 'danger' sign planted beside the hole.
